title: AI phases at a glance: events, markets, usage and compute
summary: The AI evolution table by decade, the phases table on market size, usage, availability and compute, and the four key highlights.

chunks.heading: The AI evolution table
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck summarises the whole history in one table. Learn it row by row:

| Decade | Phase | Key events & milestones |
|---|---|---|
| 1950s to 1960s | Birth of AI | Turing Test proposed (1950); Dartmouth Conference (1956); early ML programs |
| 1970s | Early Hopes & Limitations | Rule-based systems; start of the first AI Winter due to unmet expectations |
| 1980s | Expert Systems Era | Rise of expert systems; knowledge engineering gains traction |
| 1990s | AI Rebounds | Deep Blue beats Kasparov (1997); progress in NLP and speech recognition |
| 2000s | ML Matures | Rise of algorithms like SVMs and decision trees; deep learning coined (2006) |
| 2010s | Deep Learning Revolution | AlexNet (2012) revolutionizes image recognition; GANs (2014), AlphaGo (2016) |
| 2020s | Foundation & Generative AI | LLMs like GPT-3, ChatGPT, DALL·E, Codex; AI regulations & IndiaAI Mission (2024) |
chunks.exam_line: Seven phases: Birth of AI, Early Hopes & Limitations, Expert Systems Era, AI Rebounds, ML Matures, Deep Learning Revolution, Foundation & Generative AI.

chunks.heading: Phases by market size and usage
chunks.explanation_md:
A second table looks at each phase through a business lens. First, **market size** and **primary usage**:

| Phase | Period | Market size & growth | Primary usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Birth of AI | 1950s to 1960s | Mostly academic, minimal commercial investment | Symbolic AI, Turing Test, early chatbots (ELIZA) |
| Rule-based / Expert Systems | 1970s to 1980s | Grew into a **billion-dollar expert systems industry** by late 1980s | Industrial/domestic rule-based systems, diagnostics, ELIZA/PROLOG |
| AI Winter & ML Emergence | 1990s | Funding dropped; AI pivots to ML; **~$8 billion industry** by mid-2000s | Data mining, logistics, industrial automation, speech/NLP |
| ML & Deep Learning Rise | 2000s to 2010s | AI market **~$279 b in 2024**, projected **$1.8 t by 2030**; DL market **$125 b in 2025** | Web personalization, search engines, speech, image recognition |
| Deep Learning & Generative AI | 2010s to 2020s | DL market **~93 b (2024) to ~$1.42 t (2034)**, **CAGR ~31 to 35%** | ImageNet, GANs, AlphaGo (2016), ChatGPT, DALL·E |
chunks.exam_line: Market: about $8 billion by mid-2000s; AI market ~$279 b in 2024, projected $1.8 t by 2030; DL market ~93 b (2024) to ~$1.42 t (2034).

chunks.heading: Phases by availability and compute
chunks.explanation_md:
Now the same phases by **who could access AI** and **what powered it**:

| Phase | Availability / access | Compute power & data |
|---|---|---|
| Birth of AI | Limited to research labs/universities | Basic mainframes; extremely low compute & data capacity |
| Rule-based / Expert Systems | Business adoption by large firms; Lisp machines, specialized hardware | Modest compute; knowledge-engineering intensive |
| AI Winter & ML Emergence | Hidden in software back-ends; no "AI" label | Emergence of commodity PCs; larger datasets |
| ML & Deep Learning Rise | SaaS, cloud, APIs via AWS, Google, Microsoft | GPUs, clusters, big data; 2012 breakthrough (AlexNet) |
| Deep Learning & Generative AI | LLMs released to public, APIs, consumer apps; **democratized AI** | Massive transformer models; hyperscaler infrastructure investments |

Read down the access column and you see AI moving from research labs, to large firms, to hidden back-ends, to cloud APIs, to the public.
chunks.exam_line: Access went from research labs, to large firms, to hidden back-ends, to cloud APIs, to public LLMs; compute went from basic mainframes to GPUs and big data to massive transformer models.

chunks.heading: Key highlights: four shifts
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck's **key highlights** compress the table into four shifts:
1. **Markets are skyrocketing**: the total AI market exceeded **$279 b in 2024**, and DL alone is poised for **$1+ trillion by 2034**.
2. **Usage shifted** from academic/government labs to industrial applications, then to widespread commercial use, ending in **consumer-grade tools and enterprise-level deployments**.
3. **Availability evolved** from exclusive mainframes and specialized hardware to **accessible cloud services (AWS, Azure, etc.)** and later to **freely available APIs and consumer software**.
4. **Compute & data advanced** from basic mainframes to **powerful GPU clusters**; today's architectures, like **transformers**, demand immense computational resources from **hyperscalers**.
chunks.exam_line: Four shifts: markets skyrocketing ($279 b in 2024), usage from labs to consumers, availability from mainframes to cloud and APIs, compute from mainframes to GPU clusters.
